caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 67 of 2000
lawyer:
For Petitioners: Mr. Abdul Malek, Senior Advocate, (Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman, Advocate with him), instructed by Mr. Shamsul Haque Siddique, Advocate-on-Record. 

For respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Jalaluddin Choudhury and others ------ Petitioners
-Versus-
The State and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mahmudul Amin Choudhury, J:- Petitioners seek leave to appeal against judgment and order dated 6.4.2000 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2150 of 2000 summarily rejecting the same filed under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. The short fact leading to this petition is that respondent No. 2 Shamsur Rahman filed Complaint Case No. 241 of 1997 before the Cognizance Magistrate, Sadar, Jessore against the petitioners and others alleging that petitioner Nos. 1-2 carried on business in the firm name of Chowdhury Traders at Amla Bazar, Kushtia and the said firm got allotment of 1000 Metric Tons of Urea Fertilizer at the rate of Tk. 3,725/- per Metric Ton from Zia Fertilizer Factory. That allotment was sold in advance to respondent No. 2 at Tk. 41,00,000/- who paid Tk. 37,25,000/- by a demand draft towards payment of the price of the fertilizer and agreed to pay balance amount of Tk. 3,75,000/- to the petitioners upon delivery of the fertilizer to respondent No. 2 but that delivery was not made over for which Title Suit No. 3 of 1996 was filed by respondent No. 2 against the present petitioners. It is the case of the petitioners that Zia Fertilizer Company paid back the money to respondent No. 3 and not to respondent No. 2. The petitioner also failed to pay back the money to the complainant for which the present complaint was filed under Sections 406/418/420/109 of the Penal Code. The petition of complaint was sent to the District Anti-Corruption Officer. Jessore for investigation who on completion of the same submitted a report to the Cognizance’s Magistrate on 12.1.1998 stating that during investigation he found complicity of one Siddique Rahman and another Shamsul Alam of Zia Fertilizer Factory and as these two persons are public servants the case is to be tried by the Special Judge, Jessore. The Cognizance Magistrate sent the case to the learned Sessions Judge and Senior Special Judge, Jessore where it was registered as Special Case No. 10 of 1998. The learned Senior Special Judge on 30.8.1998 took cognizance of the case and ordered issuance of warrant of arrest against the accused petitioners. There after the learned Additional Sessions Judge. 1st Court and Special Judge, Court No. 2, Jessore framed charge under Sections 406/409/467/468/477/109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 on 30.11.1999. It is the further case of the petitioners that before framing of the charge the petitioners raised objection on 28.7.1999 that the case cannot proceed without obtaining sanction from the proper authority as at least two public servants have been implicated in the case but the same was not considered. Thereafter the petitioners moved the High Court Division in the aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Case under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and prayed for quashment of the proceeding wherein a Rule was issued but subsequently it was discharged. 

 3. Mr. Abdul Malek, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that as two of the accused petitioners are public servant cognizance cannot be taken without prior sanction from the proper authority. It is submitted that in the present case no sanction was obtained by the prosecution and the learned Senior Special Judge also took no step to obtain sanction before taking cognizance and as such the cognizance taken is illegal which is a violation of the provision of Section 6(5) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. It is also submitted that the Additional Sessions Judge and Special Court No. 2 also committed illegality in framing charge against all the accused persons including the petitioners without obtaining sanction to prosecute public servants which is a condition precedent and as such the proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 4. The simple question in this petition is whether such a criminal proceeding under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 can proceed against a public servant without prior sanction from the appropriate authority. The consistent view of higher courts of this country including this Division is that for prosecuting a public servant prior sanction of the appropriate authority is very much necessary and the learned Senior Special Judge cannot take cognizance without such sanction. Latest decision of this Division on this point is in the case of Abdur Rahim @ Md. Abdur Rahim Vs. The Stale 48 DIR (AD) 167, considering various decisions of different courts of this sub-continent this Division has held: 

 “The imperative language of this proviso "the Special Judge shall, immediately on receipt of the complaint" leaves no manner of doubt that before any step is taken the Special Judge has to address the Government in case of sanction not being accompanied with a petition of complaint". 

 From this it is abundantly clear that on receipt of a complaint or charge sheet as the case may be the learned Senior Special Judge should find out whether sanction from the appropriate authority for prosecuting a public servant has been obtained or not. If there is sanction to prosecute then the Senior Special Judge may proceed further by taking cognizance of the case. In the present case the police his submitted a report against two public servants and there is nothing on record to show that sanction was obtained by the prosecuting agency before submitting police report. It further appears from order dated 13.8.1998 passed by the learned Senior Special Judge that he received the record but there is nothing to indicate that the police report included sanction from the Government for prosecuting the two public servants. It further appears from order dated 30.8.1998 that the learned Senior Special Judge took cognizance of the offence. Here also there is no mention of any sanction. It is well settled that for prosecuting a public servant prior anction from the Government is a condition precedent. The Senior Special Judge is not permitted to take cognizance or to proceed further with such a case without sanction from the appropriate authority. Section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act provided that previous sanction of the Government shall be required for the prosecution of a public servant for an offence under this Act and such sanction shall be sufficient for the prosecution of a public servant for an offence. The Act further provided that in case where the complaint or report referred to in sub-section (4) of Section 4 is not accompanied by such sanction the Senior Special Judge shall immediately on receipt of the complaint or report address a letter to the Government for according sanction and if the required sanction is neither received nor refused within 60 days of the receipt of the letter by the Government such sanction shall be deemed to have been duly accorded. So where the prosecution report does not indicate of obtaining sanction to the prosecution of a public servant cognizance cannot be taken. But the proviso to Section 6(5) has given authority to the Senior Special Judge to send a letter to the appropriate authority for getting sanction and if no response is received within 60 days from the date of receipt of the letter by the Government then it should be deemed to have been duly accorded. 

 5. In the present case it appears that the prosecution report was not accompanied with such a sanction. The learned Senior Special Judge has not asked for sanction from the appropriate authority but straight way took cognizance of the case. Further it appears that when the case was sent to the court of Additional Sessions Judge and Second Court of Special Judge. Jessore charge was framed on 30.11.1999 but in view of the aforesaid decision of this Division the case cannot proceed without obtaining sanction to prosecute two public servants along with others. In view of the consistent decisions of this Division on the matter of taking of cognizance the framing of the change on the aforesaid date is found to be wholly unsustainable as the Senior Special Judge has failed to comply with the requirement of law as provided under Section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act and the High Court Division has failed to take a correct view in the matter and wrongly rejected the criminal miscellaneous case. But from the perusal of the available materials we are of the view that the accused persons should not be let off on such a technical ground. In such a situation we are inclined to interfere in the matter even without granting leave by exercising the inherent power as provided under Article 104 of the Constitution and set aside the order of taking cognizance and framing of the charge and direct the learned Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Jessore to send back the record to the Senior Special Judge for taking appropriate step as provided under Section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act which we feel necessary for end of justice. Therefore though we dismiss this petition but we set aside the order dated 30.11.1999 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge framing charge against the petitioners and others and also set aside the order dated 30.8.1998 passed by the learned Senior Special Judge in taking cognizance of the offence and we direct the learned Senior Special Judge to proceed in accordance with law.
